content:
alex: heads up — getting a cluster of customer reports + SLO alerts for hosted-infer in euw2. p99 token latency and 5xx spikes since ~10:12 UTC. support case #7891 mentioned timeouts from our API
svc-monitor: [ALERT] hosted-infer.euw2.p99_latency > 10s for 3m; error_rate(5xx) up 0.8% over baseline :rotating_light:
maria: cc @alex @jordan — any idea if this is the new batcher rollout? saw higher retransmits earlier
jordan: i'm on it, pulling traces. initial look: big trace gaps for prefetched requests, KV cache hits drop during the window
casey: support-bot forwarded a bunch of customer traces: attaching minimal repro logs they sent:
```
POST /v1/generate 500 10.8s host=api.redwood-infer.com region=euw2 model=redwood-open-1
X-Request-Id: rq_abc123
client-retries: 2
```
luis: quick sanity — did we roll kernel/quant changes to euw2 yesterday night? deployment list shows batcher-v2:ver=2026-03-16. maybe correlated
alex: timeline: batcher-v2 rolled 02:30 UTC, autoscaler tweak 08:00 UTC, prefetched KV caching enabled 09:30 UTC
maria: dashboard links: https://console/redwood/dashboards/hosted-infer/euw2/top_errors and traces: https://traces/redwood/euw2?span=serve
jordan: looking at span durations — serve span p95 ~1.1s, but p99 jumps to 9-12s and then abruptly ends with no downstream spans (trace gap). suggests proxy closed connection or timeout at gateway
casey: query i ran (logs):
```
{service="hosted-infer" region="euw2"} |= "5.." | json | top 50 by status_code
```
shows a cluster of 502/504 around 10:12-10:18 UTC from ingress proxies
luis: possible causes: backend overload (batcher backlog), proxy keepalive saturation, or auth-layer retries causing tail latency. check ingress proxy error rate and keepalive metrics
alex: can we confirm if it's customer-specific? support case says multiple customers across orgs A and B, not single tenant — points to infra-level
svc-monitor: note: routing fallback triggered 12 times in window — requests redirected to cold model variants to try to stay served
maria: repro attempt: small curl test to /v1/generate with long prompt produced a 504 after 11s from euw2. same curl to usw2 returns 200 in 400ms.
jordan: stack traces show batcher worker queue length spike then restart events on some hosts. suspect a memgrowth GC pause or OOM-kill earlier causing backlog and retransmits
casey: immediate mitigations proposed:
- temporarily disable prefetch/KV caching in euw2
- increase gateway upstream timeout from 10s -> 20s for hosted-infer routes
- roll back batcher-v2 in euw2 to previous stable
- enable canary routing to usc region for new requests
which do we want to try first? :thinking_face:
luis: prefer fastest/least-risk = increase upstream timeout + disable prefetch. rollback is heavier and needs oncall approval
alex: agree. do timeout + disable prefetch. jordan + casey can you patch config and redeploy? I will notify support and customers with ETA
maria: making dashboard panels to show impact. will monitor p99 and 5xx. notifying postmortem channel after triage
jordan: applying config: patching gateway config now — disabling prefetch flag for euw2 and bumping timeout to 20s. will post deploy ts
casey: gateway config change deployed at 3950006825 — rolling restart of small subset
jordan: second deploy (all gateways) completed at 3950006872 — getting stabilization signals
svc-monitor: [RECOVERY] hosted-infer.euw2.p99_latency back under SLO threshold at 3950006900 :white_check_mark:
alex: nice. support-bot: flag support case #7891 as mitigated and ask for confirmation from affected customers
support-bot: done — notified customers and marked pending confirmation
maria: for follow-up we need: full tracing gap analysis, host-level OOM/GC logs for batcher hosts, and correlation with batcher-v2 rollout. also propose running a stress replay on dev to reproduce queue spike
luis: assigning follow-ups to eng-runtime and eng-sre; will prep a rollback playbook if rollback still needed
alex: thanks everyone. i'll keep thread open until we have root cause.👍
